summary_md:
# AI-nervøsiteten er tilbage

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-10-30  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish Millionærklubben Q&A episode centres on renewed AI nervousness after results from Amazon, Intel and SanDisk, with panelists seeing rotation from tech into defensive consumer and healthcare stocks. Lars Svendsen is notably bearish: he cites stretched US valuations, says the big downturn has started, and holds about 14% cash personally and 20-26% in Verdensfirmaerne, while favouring peace-and-recovery cyclicals such as AFRY, Peab and building materials. Michelle Nørgaard stays constructive on Tomra long term and is selective on Vertex and Gubra.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 TOM — Tomra | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Michelle: strong Q3 is first proof of turnaround; good to own for patient investors, or keep on a candidate list.

#### Reasoning

Michelle Nørgaard (panelist) sees Q3 as the first documented turnaround after a hard-hit share price. Long-term drivers: UK deposit system, which management calls the biggest opportunity since Germany; a German replacement cycle into 2029; and recycling cost cuts expected to reach earnings next year. She stresses further proof is needed that the turn is durable.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the turnaround proves short-lived
- if the UK deposit system is delayed again
- if recycling cost savings fail to reach earnings

> *"Der er ingen tvivl om, at den her casing, hvis man er tålmodig, så tror jeg stadig, at den er rigtig, rigtig god at have på ens portefølje."*

---

### 🟢 AFRY — AFRY | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Lars has bought the engineering consultant, positioning for peace in Europe and an economic recovery.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen (panelist) says investors should look at what benefits when peace and an upswing arrive in Europe, including construction-related businesses. He has personally bought AFRY, a Nordic consulting engineer with 16,000 staff, after Persson discussed it. The view is thematic; no valuation or earnings detail was given.

#### Sell Triggers

- if peace in Ukraine does not materialise
- if the European recovery fails to arrive

> *"jeg har jo købt en over, som Persson har stået og fortalt om, den hedder Afry."*

---

### 🟠 PEAB-B — Peab | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

On Lars's list as preferred Swedish contractor for a peace-and-recovery theme, but not bought; Persson says the signal isn't there yet.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen plans to buy Peab soon as his contractor pick for a European recovery, citing its Danish asphalt work near Hillerød. Persson, a colleague who uses technical signals, has repeatedly advised that the signal is absent, which is why it remains a watch rather than an executed buy.

#### Sell Triggers

- if peace and recovery do not materialise
- if the technical signal Persson awaits never appears

> *"Men det er P-UP. Det er min, jeg har ikke købt den endnu. Men den står altså på listen."*

---

### 🟢 PHO — Photocure | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Lars recently added near 46 after reading the report; US progress, margin focus and cash, with a potentially large Asieris product. Wants 150.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen keeps backing Photocure and bought more around NOK 46. The report showed slow progress, US gains and margin improvement, with NOK 160m in the bank to fund the legal dispute. Asieris disputes the full milestone payment on the cervical product, and he believes it is trying to squeeze Photocure and buy it cheaply. His NOK 150 target depends on the product's potential.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Photocure loses the Asieris dispute
- if cash runs short for legal costs
- if US progress stalls

> *"Jeg har sat sig på, at vi skal have 150 for den."*

---

### 🟢 BAKKA — Bakkafrost | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Lars has bought it as a preferred end-of-chain salmon producer that makes its own feed; long-term food demand supports it.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen holds Bakkafrost, up about 5% in nearly a year, on the view that growing populations favour food and salmon. He prefers the end of the value chain to feed makers, and Bakkafrost also produces its own feed. Michelle Nørgaard flagged rising fish-feed costs as a possible margin risk.

#### Sell Triggers

- if feed costs squeeze margins
- if salmon prices fall to the low end of their range

> *"Mener man skal være i endeled"*

---

### 🟢 LSG — Lerøy Seafood | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Lars owns it as part of his two-stock salmon position; long-term demand for food supports the case.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen holds Lerøy alongside Bakkafrost, up about 5% so far, and likes salmon producers on long-term population and food demand. He prefers end producers over feed companies. Rising feed costs, raised by Michelle Nørgaard, are the main margin concern.

#### Sell Triggers

- if feed costs squeeze margins
- if salmon prices weaken

> *"det er Bakkerfrost og lige over i Seafood, LSG er den kode"*

---

### 🟡 TRIFOR — Trifork | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Lars holds it; report looked sensible, growth was good and guidance range was kept, with AI implementation a possible demand driver.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen owns Trifork and admits he is biased as a holder and has not read the report in detail. Growth looked good and the company stayed within its promised range after two weak years of retaining staff in a soft market. The thesis is that companies will need Trifork to implement AI in practice. Lars said the recovery now appears to be coming.

#### Sell Triggers

- if growth fades again
- if AI implementation demand fails to materialise

> *"Men jeg synes, at han er på. Han holder kursen"*

---

### 🔴 TRMD-A — Torm | **SELL** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 70%

Lars says Verdensfirmaerne will probably sell Torm soon, taking cash to about 33% as he turns defensive.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen is raising cash because he considers US equities extremely expensive and sees the big downturn as having begun. Selling Torm, expected soon, would lift Verdensfirmaerne's cash to about 33%. The sale is presented as part of portfolio de-risking; no Torm-specific negative view was given.

> *"og når vi får solgt tormen, vil vi nok snart skal gøre. så kommer vi op på 33 procent cash."*

---

### ⛔ SCHO — Schouw & Co | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 75%

Verdensfirmaerne sold it; Lars objects to the BioMar spin-off structure and says management must now show proper conduct.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen calls Schouw a sensibly run company but sold it because management retained half of BioMar and sold the rest rather than distributing the shares to owners. He sees that as keeping shareholders' money with management and undermining trust. He places the company in the penalty box until it behaves properly.

#### Sell Triggers

- if management shows better shareholder conduct, the avoid view would no longer hold

> *"Så skov er du ikke lige huskåret? Nej, det er jeg ikke."*

---

### ⛔ BIOMAR — BioMar | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Lars would rather own Norwegian salmon producers than BioMar, since farmers can make their own feed and capture the profit there.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen acknowledges BioMar's high feed prices make it a good business, but questions its position because salmon farmers can build their own feed units. Norway's special salmon tax also pushes farmers to book profits in feed. He says he would prefer actual salmon producers, though he also notes salmon strength helps BioMar.

#### Sell Triggers

- if farmers do not insource feed and BioMar keeps its pricing

> *"Jeg vil hellere købe rigtig laksaks op i Norge, end Biomar, som laver fodret."*

---

### ⛔ RR — Rolls-Royce | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Panel steers a listener away: Lars sees it well paid for after its recovery; Michelle notes cyclicality and would look elsewhere for diversification.

#### Reasoning

For a 3-5 year holding, Lars Svendsen thinks the shares have rerun too far and are richly priced, requiring big visions. Michelle Nørgaard calls it a good long-term case but cyclical, tied to flight hours and service contracts, and would rather diversify into consumer, financial or utility stocks. The listener's existing exposure was also considered.

#### Sell Triggers

- if valuation falls enough to no longer be richly priced

> *"Altså meget godt betalt. Det må vi sige."*

---

### 🟠 GUBRA — Gubra | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Michelle would only dip a toe, as it pairs a small contract research unit with a pipeline option; Lars bought after the event news. Report 6 Nov.

#### Reasoning

Michelle Nørgaard sees a low P/E, a UCN2 programme in human trials and upcoming catalysts, including the 6 November report and a planned phase 2 trial, but warns against buying simply because it looks cheap. Lars Svendsen bought after the company announced its first-ever investor event and sees own-account development as a sign of strength. Views differ on sizing.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the 6 November report disappoints on pipeline progress
- if UCN2 trial data disappoint

> *"Jeg vil ikke bare kaste mig hovedkølet ind, fordi jeg siger, at den er billig"*

---

### 🟠 VRTX — Vertex Pharmaceuticals | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 60%

Michelle: FDA decision in late November is the key catalyst, but stock is near highs and near-term catalysts look priced in.

#### Reasoning

Michelle Nørgaard cites October data showing a 52% reduction in urine protein at 36 weeks and an FDA decision due in late November. The shares are not cheap, trade close to the top and largely price in near-term catalysts. Buying rests on the cystic fibrosis franchise continuing to perform, plus the pipeline in kidney disease and pain. She mentions it as a healthcare idea to consider.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the FDA decision is negative
- if the cystic fibrosis business weakens

> *"Så det er det, man skal være og holde øje med."*

---

### 🟠 NDA — Aurubis | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Lars would not buy at 134 but doubts it breaks 100 and will revisit it; Michelle watches guidance in the 2 December annual report.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen sold at 125, having bought near 65-70, and says he has no desire to buy at about 134, though he doubts it breaks below 100. Copper is volatile and expensive. Michelle Nørgaard links the fall to copper and raw-material margin concerns, and sees the 2 December report and guidance as the test of whether sentiment can reverse.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the 2 December guidance disappoints
- if shares break below 100

> *"Jeg tror ikke, jeg har lyst til at købe Auerbus på 134"*

---

### 🟠 SZG — Salzgitter | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Neutral | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Lars is considering it as an indirect route into Aurubis, adding a steel business, and will look further before next week.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen notes Salzgitter is Aurubis's owner, with its stake near its market value, so a buyer also gets the steelworks, which is pursuing green steel with state funding. He says he wants to study it further; no decision has been made.

> *"Så jeg vil gerne begynde at kigge på den ud."*

---

### 🟠 LEG — LEG Immobilien | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Cheap but needs falling long German yields; Lars calls the sector's valuation an oddity and says shares could double when it turns.

#### Reasoning

Michelle Nørgaard says German residential stocks trade like bonds, so a rerating depends on lower long German yields, and calls LEG cheap for a reason. Lars Svendsen finds the low valuation strange and has no explanation, but says investors should jump aboard once it truly turns because it could double.

#### Sell Triggers

- if long German yields keep rising

> *"Aktien, den er billig, men den er også billigere end grund."*

---

### ⛔ NCOD — Norcod | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Lars calls the cod farmer a nightmare and belly flop, though he says he does not follow it closely.

#### Reasoning

Asked whether a listener's rising cod farmer resembles a salmon-style adventure, Lars Svendsen says he does not follow it but has heard complaints from investors and cannot see how it would recover. Michelle Nørgaard offers no company-specific view. The stance is low-conviction and based on past performance.

> *"Ja, nej, jeg føler ikke med i Nordkort. Det har været et mareridt."*

---

### 🟠 HH — H+H International | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Lars names it as a building-recovery idea with a takeover angle via Solbet's roughly 28% block.

#### Reasoning

Lars Svendsen says investors should look at construction and building components ahead of peace and recovery, calling H+H a tinderbox. Solbet holds about 28% and has asked authorities about going higher; if refused, it could sell the block to a major such as Heidelberg or CRH. He did not say he owns or is buying it.

#### Sell Triggers

- if no bid or block sale materialises
- if the European construction recovery is delayed

> *"Altså hvis ham dernede, Sol B eller hvad den hedder nede i, eller Sol Bet"*

---
